source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary on NFIL: 'Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits NFIL's export-led business'; global manufacturers are increasingly sourcing specialty chemicals and fluorochemicals from India to reduce dependence on Chinese suppliers, and NFIL (HPP, CDMO/CRAMS, specialty chemicals) is cited as a beneficiary of this diversification trend. CDMO segment is reported as ~98% overseas / ~2% India revenue mix, underscoring export/global-client orientation.

'Unprecedented capex plans to further augment capacities besides preparing for growing opportunities arising due to China plus one factor... building capacities in a few more niche APIs as per the evolving demand scenario in the backdrop of China plus one opportunities and upcoming opportunity size of ~US$20 billion in molecules going off-patent over FY23-25.' Company earmarked ~Rs 1000-2000 crore capex (incl. greenfield Kakinada plant) to capture this opportunity.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material and solvent costs (petrochemical-derivative inputs) rose alongside an 'energy crisis in China'; imports account for around 45% of raw material consumption, providing a natural partial hedge. Company mitigates via backward integration, solvent recovery and diversified sourcing (reduced China dependence) rather than disclosing a specific crude-linked raw material percentage.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Contracts with major clients at fixed exchange rates (currency-fluctuation impact shared with customers); discretionary forward-contract hedging 'as and when required', with continuous monitoring of currency volatility impact on cost structure.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Divi's has entered contracts with major clients at fixed exchange rates, where the impact of currency fluctuations is shared by both parties... undertakes hedging transactions as and when required.' Net foreign-currency asset exposure was ₹2,006 crore as on 31 March 2025, vs ₹1,521 crore as on 31 March 2024.

govt_capex.evidence: 'The ongoing government-driven infrastructure expansion in India (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing) is expected to fuel robust demand for steel, stainless steel, and aluminium products, providing a long-term tailwind for volume growth' -- cited as a demand driver in company/analyst commentary; no specific % of revenue tied to government projects disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company deleveraged sharply: debt fell to ₹10.8 billion (Sep 2024) from ₹19.8 billion a year earlier, against ₹12.3 billion cash, i.e. a net cash position of ~₹1.54 billion (CRISIL AA/Stable rated), and a ₹2,700 crore FY25-29 expansion capex was stated to be funded entirely from internal cash flows with no new debt -- suggesting low incremental floating-rate exposure, though no explicit floating-vs-fixed split was disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: 'Shyam Metalics Flat Products has been selected to invest under the PLI scheme for specialty steel' -- part of the Government of India's ₹6,322 crore PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (FY2023-24 to FY2027-28); revenue contribution/percentage not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company/analyst commentary notes 'growth in export markets within the Distribution Solutions division' contributed to Q4 CY2024 revenue momentum, alongside a primary 'local for local' strategy across 23 market segments; no explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification framing was found in sources reviewed -- narrative is domestic-manufacturing-for-India-market rather than export-diversification-from-China.

rural.evidence: 'Rural outreach program launched in seven states, testing over 110,000 patients in underserved regions' (as of Q1 FY27); deepening presence in Tier-3/Tier-4 markets via franchisees cited as a key growth lever. Tier-3 cities saw a 2% rise in revenue alongside a 61% increase in number of collection centres and 53% rise in PUPs (patient utility points) in suburban settings -- no aggregate rural revenue % of total disclosed in sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: Government schemes -- Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) and PM-ABHIM -- are cited industry-wide as demand drivers expanding diagnostics access across Tier-2/Tier-3 regions; no specific % of Dr Lal PathLabs' own revenue attributed to government scheme partnerships was found in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Coverage of United Spirits' cost base cites glass bottle inflation (~12-15%, with some reports of 11-17%), PET resin/cap costs up 30-50%/15-20%, and paper carton costs up sharply; commentary links crude oil price moves (geopolitical tensions in West Asia) to higher packaging and energy costs, but no company-disclosed % of raw material cost tied to crude was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Third-party company-profile data states 'India accounts for 99.6% of net sales' for United Spirits, implying minimal direct export/FX revenue exposure; the company's emerging-markets export business (Africa/Asia) is described as a small initiative. Year of this specific stat could not be confirmed against a specific annual report.

OFSS risk disclosures (as summarized via search of its annual reports) state market risk 'mainly comprises foreign currency risk' and that the company 'engages in transactions in foreign currency with customers from abroad which are settled shortly, reducing any foreign exchange risk'; specific hedge/forward-contract % of receivables was not found in accessible sources. Note: OFSS is overwhelmingly an export-of-software-services business (global banking clients) but a current FY24-25 India-vs-overseas revenue split could not be confirmed -- an old FY2021-22 quarterly regional split (US ~28%, Europe ~18%, MEA ~20%, APAC ~26% of revenue) appeared in a broker note but is stale and was not used to populate the numeric fields.

china_plus_one.evidence: Broader industry/press commentary (The Ken, Forbes India) frames China+1 as a driver for Indian API makers, and notes Glenmark hived off its API business into a separate entity, Glenmark Life Sciences, in 2018-19 as 'the China-plus-one story began to emerge.' Because the API business (where the China+1 narrative most directly applies, e.g. ~70% of India's APIs historically imported from China) now sits in the separately-listed Glenmark Life Sciences rather than in Glenmark Pharmaceuticals' own formulations-led export business, no explicit China+1 framing tied to Glenmark Pharmaceuticals' (GLENMARK) own revenue growth was found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Analyst commentary notes 'a large part of Glenmark's revenue comes from exports and hence the company faces risk of currency fluctuations' and that the company carries 'a debt-heavy balance sheet with the majority of its debt denominated in foreign exchange.' A Glenmark subsidiary's (Poland, sp. z o.o.) standalone filing states it 'does not use hedge accounting' for embedded derivatives, marking them to fair value through P&L, but this is subsidiary-level, not confirmed as group-wide consolidated policy, so usd_revenue_pct and hedging_policy were left null pending direct AR confirmation.

pli_scheme.evidence: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals is listed among the domestic companies approved in Group A of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (per Department of Pharmaceuticals PLI-approved applicant list, alongside Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr Reddy's, Aurobindo, Lupin, Torrent, Intas, etc.). Revenue benefit as a % of total revenue was not disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: Demand-driver commentary tied to APL Apollo's expansion plans cites 'increased construction activities across residential, commercial, and government infrastructure projects' and, more broadly for the steel-tube industry, 'domestic water infrastructure, oil exploration and transportation, construction, irrigation, infrastructure, and expansion of gas pipelines such as national gas grid and city gas distribution.' The Raipur brownfield expansion (600 KT) is specifically described as targeting 'the emerging infrastructure opportunity in railway stations and airport terminals.' No revenue % tied to government capex specifically was disclosed in sources found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt reported to have fallen to roughly Rs 4 billion in FY25 from about Rs 8 billion in FY24 (a ~48% decline per third-party annual-report analysis); no floating-vs-fixed rate split was found in sources found.

pli_scheme.evidence: APL Apollo Tubes was not found among the confirmed signatories in coverage of the Ministry of Steel's Specialty Steel PLI Scheme 1.1 MoU signings (42 MoUs / 25 companies, announced March 2025); no public confirmation of APL Apollo's participation in any PLI scheme was found. Company growth narrative centers on domestic infrastructure/construction demand rather than PLI incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films is described as 'India's largest exporter of polyester films' (Plexcouncil top-exporter award for 33 consecutive years), exporting 'over 70 per cent of its production to over 80 countries,' with SunControl window films up 37.6% YoY and PPF business up 25% YoY 'driven by new products, expanded market reach, and global demand.' No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification framing tied to this export growth was found in sources searched -- growth is attributed to product launches and market expansion, not to customers diversifying away from China.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company profile notes: 'Raw material prices fluctuate with changes in crude oil prices'; primary raw materials are petrochemicals (Purified Terephthalic Acid, Mono-ethylene glycol, polypropylene). Garware Hi-Tech Films is backward-integrated into PET chip manufacturing and procures inputs from Indian refiners such as Reliance Industries 'at import parity prices,' directly linking its cost base to global crude/PET benchmarks, though no company-disclosed % of raw material cost was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company is described as mitigating volatile raw-material prices and forex exposure 'with forward contracts and long term agreements' -- specific % hedged not disclosed in sources found.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue was 77.6% of sales in FY24 (up from 67.1% in FY23); a quarterly geographic revenue split (~Q2 FY25) shows Americas ~55%, India ~19%, Others ~14%, Europe ~12% of total revenue, i.e. the large majority of revenue is USD/foreign-currency denominated via exports, mainly to the US.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed evidence found of Garware Hi-Tech Films Ltd (GRWRHITECH) itself participating in a PLI scheme. Note: search results also surfaced 'Garware Technical Fibres Ltd,' a separate, differently-listed company (technical yarns/geosynthetics) referenced in PLI-for-textiles coverage -- this was NOT treated as evidence for GRWRHITECH to avoid conflating the two distinct Garware entities.

COFORGE.notes: AR PDF and screener.in / coforge.com / news.coforge.com / icicidirect.com were all blocked by the environment's egress proxy (EGRESS_BLOCKED on every domain tried, including en.wikipedia.org, confirming a near-total WebFetch outage this session). Data derived from WebSearch result snippets/summaries of press releases and broker notes citing FY25 geographic segment mix (Americas/EMEA/RoW). Coforge is a pure IT services exporter; rural, govt_capex, crude_exposure, pli_scheme and rate_sensitive are correctly null as these signals are not typically disclosed/applicable for this business model. A Q1FY26 hedging/mark-to-market loss data point was found but excluded as it falls outside the FY2024-25 report period and lacked a verifiable AR-linked hedging policy quote.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix disclosed in Q4FY25 results presentation: US Formulations 45%, India Formulations 26%, International Markets Formulations (Europe & Emerging Markets combined) 13%, Consumer Wellness 11%, Medtech 3%, APIs 2%, Alliances 0.2% of consolidated revenue of ~Rs 2,32,415 mn.

ZYDUSLIFE.notes: zyduslife.com, nsearchives.nseindia.com and www.screener.in were all blocked by the environment's egress proxy; could not read the full AR PDF (link found: https://www.zyduslife.com/investor/admin/uploads/14/2/2024-2025.pdf, also on NSE archives). Geography figures derived from Q4FY25 results presentation segment mix via WebSearch synthesis (domestic = India Formulations + Consumer Wellness; export = US Formulations + International Markets + residual Medtech/API/Alliances). China+1 and hedging-policy claims surfaced in search were generic/third-party (PESTLE-style analysis sites) without a verifiable company-specific AR quote, so left null per the do-not-invent rule. PLI participation could not be confirmed with a reliable source specific to Zydus.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Anthem Biosciences is distinguished by its 'China-plus-one' strategy, having built a supply chain with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials", sourcing less than 20% of inputs from China. CEO Ajay Bhardwaj: "We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones." Company positioned in IPO/DRHP-linked commentary (incl. Frost & Sullivan market report filed with the DRHP) as a direct beneficiary of global biotech/pharma clients diversifying CDMO sourcing away from China, with FY24/FY25 revenue growth of 34% and 29% attributed partly to this trend plus capacity ramp-up.

ANTHEM.notes: Anthem IPO'd in July 2025; no full post-IPO Annual Report was locatable via search (screener.in and bseindia.com blocked/inaccessible). Data sourced from DRHP-derived commentary, broker notes and press coverage of the IPO. Export/domestic split ('export markets account for about 75-80% of revenues') is DRHP-sourced (FY24 data primarily, carried forward as best available). CRDMO segment mix (D&M 70.78%, R&D 10.87%, Specialty ingredients 18.35% of FY25 revenue) was found but not mapped to geography since it's a business-line split, not a country/region split.

USHAMART.notes: ushamartin.com (including the direct AR PDF link found: https://ushamartin.com/upload/investorrelations/annual-report-d-2024-25.pdf) and screener.in were both blocked by the environment's egress proxy; could not read the AR MD&A, notes to accounts, or financial risk management/segment sections directly. Only high-level FY25 domestic/export split (45%/55%, 'international markets accounted for 55% of total revenues in FY25, reflecting sustained demand in oil and gas, mining and infrastructure') was recoverable via WebSearch of press coverage. Raw material for Usha Martin is iron ore/steel wire rod, not crude-oil-linked, so crude_exposure is correctly null. No China+1, rural, govt capex, rate-sensitivity, PLI, or forex-hedging disclosures could be found via search alone.

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin Point's backward integration into APIs (R&D completed for 90+ APIs) is aimed at securing its US/Global injectable and LatAm pipeline 'from any supply shock' and reducing 'dependency on China and third party external API suppliers,' targeting ~70% of US filings backward-integrated with own APIs. Framed primarily as the company's own supply-security/margin-expansion strategy rather than an explicit AR narrative of revenue growth from clients diversifying away from China.

inr_exposure.evidence: US business estimated at ~Rs 367 Cr of ~Rs 2,034 Cr total FY25 revenue (~18%), per broker/investor-presentation data; remainder mostly Latin America (76%) and Africa (3%), largely non-USD/local-currency and USD-linked distributor sales.

CAPLIPOINT.notes: caplinpoint.net, screener.in and bseindia.com were inaccessible (egress-blocked); relied on WebSearch synthesis of broker research PDFs and company earnings presentations (e.g. Q4 FY25 earnings presentation title found via search) referenced in snippets rather than reading the AR or presentation directly. Latin America (76%) and Africa (3%) revenue shares are mapped into export_other_pct since the schema has no dedicated Latin America field; domestic_pct left null as it was not explicitly stated (only inferable as a small residual).

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst coverage of KPR Mill's FY25 performance: 'KPR Mill, headquartered in Coimbatore, is a vertically integrated garment and yarn manufacturing player that is a direct and quantifiable beneficiary of the China-plus-one supply chain shift in global knitwear exports... its results consistently reflect improved global knitwear order flows as international fashion brands diversify sourcing from Chinese manufacturers.' Garment exports go primarily to reputed customers in the US, UK, Australia and other European countries; garment segment rose to 44% of consolidated operating income in FY25 (from 41% in FY24).

crude_exposure.evidence: KPR Mill's yarn/fabric portfolio includes polyester-cotton and viscose yarn and single-jersey fabric with lycra/spandex; these man-made/synthetic fibres (polyester, spandex) are petroleum-derived, giving indirect crude-oil-linked raw material exposure alongside its dominant cotton input (cotton ~42% of input cost per broker notes). No AR-disclosed % of raw material cost tied specifically to crude-linked inputs was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 export revenue was ~42% of total revenue (vs 58% domestic), with exports concentrated in garments sold to customers in the US, UK, Australia and Europe. No specific forward-cover/hedging percentage was found in available sources.

rural.evidence: Company commentary cites 'rural electrification schemes' and expansion into the North-East as a 'high-growth frontier for Finolex, with revenue doubling over the last four years,' with distribution scaling in Assam and neighbouring states tied to government-led rural electrification drives. No overall % of revenue from rural markets was disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Company-cited demand drivers include '100% electrification of existing railway networks, rural electrification schemes, public charging infrastructure, growing demand for telecom/broadband, and laying optical fibre cables under BharatNet and Smart City projects,' plus 'increased government investments in roads, railways and housing.' A ~Rs 500 crore capex programme is planned over 18-24 months. No specific % of revenue tied to government capex was disclosed in sources found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Finolex Cables has historically operated as a near debt-free/debt-free company; FY25 commentary notes finance costs down 17.7% YoY and long-term debt remaining minimal/stable. No floating-rate liability % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is a small share of the business - Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27 commentary notes exports rising from ~Rs 30 crore to ~Rs 50-52 crore per quarter, with management targeting export revenue share of only 2-3% of total revenue over the next two years, implying current export/USD exposure is well under that.

rural.evidence: GSK Pharma India's established distribution network is described as covering 'urban and rural areas, ensuring broad market penetration,' with market expansion into tier-2/tier-3 cities cited as a growth driver as private hospital/clinic reach grows there. No specific % of revenue from rural/tier-2-3 markets was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: GSK Pharma derives approximately 98% of its revenue from the domestic Indian market and about 2% from international/export markets, per broker/analyst coverage of its financials; the business is described as 'India-focused' with 'minimal international export operations.' No hedging policy specifics were found (the company likely also carries import-side forex exposure on formulations/APIs sourced from the global GSK group, but this was not quantified in sources found).

pli_scheme.evidence: GSK Pharmaceuticals India is primarily a branded-formulations marketing company (top brands include Augmentin, Calpol, Betnovate, Ceftum, Eltroxin) rather than a bulk-drug/API manufacturer; no evidence was found of GSK Pharma India being an approved participant in the Indian PLI schemes for bulk drugs/APIs or pharmaceuticals.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company/analyst commentary frames India's 'strategic proximity to key markets like ASEAN, Europe, Japan, and Korea' as 'strengthening its position as a global auto component sourcing hub,' with Uno Minda's global tier-1 partners (via 15+ JVs with German/Korean/Japanese technology partners) seeking lighting, alloys, sensors and electronics content out of India. The company's dominant narrative, however, is import substitution/localization away from China (e.g. first India-localized camera module and wireless EV chargers) rather than an explicit export-led China+1 framing.

inr_exposure.evidence: Uno Minda's revenue mix is described as ~90% domestic / ~10% international, with international/export customers spanning OEM tier-1 partners and aftermarket distributors across ASEAN and Africa. No specific hedging policy % was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: UNO Minda was one of 18 companies provisionally selected in the 3rd round of the PLI Scheme for White Goods (AC and LED-light components), committing to invest Rs 19.82 crore in the LED-lights component category. Coverage also describes Minda Industries/UNO Minda as 'PLI beneficiaries in the automobile sector for EV components.' Specific revenue benefit/% was not disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: Government scheme revenue (CGHS and state programmes) is reported by third-party analyst coverage as having risen from 11.04% of revenue in FY24 to 13.80% in FY26 (Medanta/Global Health), implying an FY25 figure somewhere between these; cash/self-pay revenue meanwhile fell from ~34.4% (FY23) to ~30.3% (FY26). Regional mix varies significantly - e.g. Lucknow described as ~85% cash+insurance with very little government-scheme business. No AR-sourced exact FY25 % was confirmed, so left unquantified pending primary-source verification.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Global Health reported gross debt of ~Rs 631 crore against a net cash surplus (~Rs 591 crore) in recent disclosures, with a planned ~Rs 4,500 crore project capex over the next five years to be funded through internal accruals and debt - implying rising future debt/rate exposure as expansion (including the Noida facility) proceeds. No floating-rate % of liabilities was found.
